why.stone: Faceted glyphic serif that reads convincingly as letters cut into stone.
why.carving: SISIFO, the titles and 62.5 show crisp polygonal facets and flat-cut curves at display size.
why.calm: Wide, steady rhythm with presence; the faceting adds texture without aggression.
why.personality: Memorable chiselled character that fits the stone and engraving brief closely.
why.inscription: Capitals (BENCH PRESS, MOBILITÀ · EQUILIBRIO) have broad Roman proportions and a dignified flared stroke.
why.oblique: A real italic with consistent slant and even colour, clearly distinct, slightly light at 13 px.
why.small: 13 px text is open and readable; the facets disappear at that size so it stays clean.

why.stone: Lapidary, glyphic wedge forms with flared strokes read convincingly as cut stone.
why.carving: Titles and set numbers show crisp polygonal facets and flat-cut curves throughout.
why.calm: Steady rhythm and moderate weight; the faceting adds texture without aggression.
why.personality: Distinct carved character that still feels refined and suits the app.
why.inscription: Capitals have Roman inscriptional proportions, flared strokes and quiet dignity.
why.oblique: A consistent, even italic clearly distinct from the upright and readable at 13 px.
why.small: 13 px text is clean and open; the glyphic forms stay smooth at that size.

why.stone: The flared, glyphic serif with faceted curves reads like a carved monument inscription.
why.carving: At display size the O, S, 6 and 5 show clean flat-cut facets and sharp flared terminals.
why.calm: It is quiet and even, with presence, and only a slight nervousness in the faceted heavy numerals.
why.personality: A memorable chiselled, classical voice that suits the app's grounded tone.
why.inscription: The capitals have wide Roman proportions, flared strokes and real inscriptional dignity.
why.oblique: The italic has a consistent slant and even colour, is clearly distinct, and reads well as emphasis.
why.small: The 13 px lines are clear and comfortable, with slightly wide spacing but nothing clotting.

why.stone: Flared glyphic sans with inscriptional ancestry gives a quiet, chiselled-sans feel.
why.carving: The flare is smooth and drawn; display letters show no cut facets.
why.calm: Very calm, even and graceful with presence and no aggression.
why.personality: Recognisable humanist-flared character that suits the app, if familiar.
why.inscription: Capitals have Roman-derived proportions and flaring, a sans echo of inscriptional letters.
why.oblique: A clean, evenly coloured sloped roman, consistent and readable, less distinct than a true italic.
why.small: 13 px text is open, sharp and comfortable.

why.stone: A flared humanist sans with a hint of glyphic stroke, grounded but not carved.
why.carving: Smooth flared strokes with no facets at display sizes.
why.calm: Light, even and open; very calm and unhurried.
why.personality: The flared stroke gives quiet distinction suited to the app.
why.inscription: Capitals echo Roman proportions through flared strokes, though sans-serif.
why.oblique: A clean, consistent italic distinct from the upright and readable at 13 px.
why.small: 13 px text is open, even and very easy to read.

why.stone: The flared sans nods to glyphic lettering but feels light and humanist rather than stone-cut.
why.carving: The stroke flare is smooth and continuous, with no facets at display sizes.
why.calm: It is calm, open and evenly paced, with no aggression.
why.personality: A pleasant, Optima-like humanist sans that is somewhat familiar.
why.inscription: The flared capitals echo inscriptional proportions and stroke modulation reasonably well.
why.oblique: The italic is consistent and readable, clearly distinct though somewhat soft.
why.small: The 13 px text is clean, open and very easy to read.

why.stone: Rough, irregular outlines give a weathered, hand-cut stone feel.
why.carving: Display titles and numbers show clear chiselled facets and broken, flat-cut curves.
why.calm: The roughness creates a nervous, uneven texture and the bold lines barely differ from regular.
why.personality: Strongly distinctive, ancient-feeling character with real imperfection.
why.inscription: Capitals have classical proportions and a weathered inscription look, though somewhat irregular.
why.oblique: Italic is distinct but a calligraphic, almost blackletter-tinged cursive that is busy and lumpy at 13 px.
why.small: 13 px lines are readable but the ragged edges soften and the colour is uneven.

why.stone: Rough, irregular outlines and old-style forms read as weathered, hand-cut lettering.
why.carving: Display sizes show clear angular facets on the bowls and figures, like chisel cuts.
why.calm: The rough edges and lively, uneven contours give a nervous, antique texture; bold barely differs from regular.
why.personality: Highly memorable rustic, imperfect character that fits the Sisyphus myth.
why.inscription: Capitals are classical with good proportion, though the roughness reads more weathered than formal.
why.oblique: A real italic with character, but its calligraphic, bouncy forms are busy at 13 px.
why.small: Readable at 13 px but the roughened edges make the text a little blotchy and uneven.

why.stone: The polygonal, slightly irregular outlines look like letters cut into rock by hand.
why.carving: SISIFO and the set numbers are made of crisp, flat facets on every curve, clearly chiselled rather than drawn.
why.calm: The texture is grounded but slightly rough and uneven, and the bold weight barely differs from regular.
why.personality: Its hand-cut, imperfect stone feel is unique and fits the Sisyphus theme closely.
why.inscription: The capitals have classical proportions and serifs, with a rustic rather than formal-imperial cut.
why.oblique: The italic is a lively calligraphic hand with an uneven, bouncy texture that is distinct but a little lumpy at 13 px.
why.small: The 13 px roman is readable and open, though the faceted outlines soften slightly at small sizes.

why.stone: Elegant high-contrast serif that feels editorial rather than carved.
why.carving: Smooth bracketed serifs and soft curves at display sizes, no facets.
why.calm: Quiet and refined with an even rhythm.
why.personality: Polished but close to a generic magazine serif.
why.inscription: Capitals have classical proportions and decent dignity, with a slightly modern contrast.
why.oblique: Well-formed true italic, consistent and distinct, readable at 13 px.
why.small: 13 px text reads well, though the thin hairlines lighten it slightly.

why.stone: An elegant transitional serif, solid and classical but smooth ink rather than stone.
why.carving: Curves are smooth with sharp hairline serifs; no facets at display sizes.
why.calm: Even, measured rhythm and balanced contrast; very quiet with presence.
why.personality: Refined and pleasant but close to a generic editorial serif.
why.inscription: Well-proportioned classical capitals, though bookish rather than lapidary.
why.oblique: A true italic with consistent slant, even colour and clear distinction from the upright.
why.small: 13 px text is even and readable, with slightly fine hairlines.

why.stone: An elegant, classical transitional serif that feels refined and bookish more than carved.
why.carving: Its display sizes have smooth curves and bracketed serifs with no chiselled facets.
why.calm: The rhythm is very even, with a quiet, composed presence.
why.personality: It is handsome but conventional, a familiar editorial serif.
why.inscription: The capitals have good classical proportions and dignity, if more typographic than inscribed.
why.oblique: A true italic with an even slant and colour, clearly distinct and graceful at 13 px.
why.small: The 13 px lines are sharp, open and very comfortable.

why.stone: Sturdy wedge-serifed humanist with weight, but it reads as a bookish slab rather than lettering cut in stone.
why.carving: Display titles and set numbers have smooth, ink-like curves; only the wedge serifs hint at a cut.
why.calm: Even, grounded rhythm with no shouting, though the bold numbers are quite dark.
why.personality: Warm, slightly condensed wedge serif with a distinct voice that suits a gentle tracker.
why.inscription: Capitals are narrow and slab-like (BENCH PRESS, SISIFO), far from Roman inscriptional proportions.
why.oblique: A true cursive italic with consistent slant and even colour, clearly distinct, slightly narrow at 13 px.
why.small: 13 px lines are crisp and readable, a little compact in width.

why.stone: A sturdy, slab-ish book face with weight and solidity, more woodcut-and-print than carved stone.
why.carving: Display letters are smooth with soft bracketed wedges; no visible facets or flat-cut curves.
why.calm: Even, compact rhythm and moderate contrast; the bold is heavy but never shouts.
why.personality: Warm wedge serifs and condensed proportions give a friendly, distinct voice.
why.inscription: Capitals are narrow and bookish, far from Roman inscriptional proportions.
why.oblique: A true, consistent italic with even colour, clearly distinct from the upright and fine at 13 px.
why.small: 13 px lines are sturdy and open, though the narrow set makes them a little tight.

why.stone: A condensed, slightly angular slab-like serif that feels sturdy and grounded but more like a book face than cut stone.
why.carving: The heavy S, O and set numbers show some flat, angled cuts on curves, but the effect is mild and mostly reads as ink.
why.calm: The narrow, dark bold and tightly packed capitals make it a little dense and insistent rather than quiet.
why.personality: The condensed, chunky, slightly rustic forms are distinctive and memorable.
why.inscription: The capitals are narrow and compressed, far from the broad, square proportions of Roman inscriptional caps.
why.oblique: A true italic with a consistent slant and clear contrast with the upright, though it reads a bit cramped at 13 px.
why.small: The 13 px lines are sharp and legible, but the narrow letters and tight spacing make them slightly dense.

why.stone: Heavy, angular old-style serif with a solid, grounded mass.
why.carving: Some angular serifs and sheared terminals at display size, but the bowls stay mostly smooth.
why.calm: Very dark colour throughout makes titles and numbers feel heavy and slightly loud.
why.personality: Distinctive, robust and slightly quirky (the open g), though more bookish than lapidary.
why.inscription: Capitals are solid and classical with good dignity, a little dense and heavy.
why.oblique: True italic with steady slant, but whole italic lines run dark at 13 px.
why.small: 13 px text is legible and sharp, if somewhat heavy in colour.

why.stone: Heavy, high-contrast forms with slightly irregular edges feel solid and stony.
why.carving: Display numbers and capitals show angular cuts on curves, though less crisp than a true glyphic.
why.calm: Very dark and heavy overall, with an oddly hooked g, so it tends toward loud.
why.personality: Strong old-style character with idiosyncratic details.
why.inscription: Capitals are dignified but heavy and condensed rather than inscriptional.
why.oblique: The italic is consistent but very bold and dark at 13 px, crowding the emphasis.
why.small: 13 px text is dark and dense; readable but heavy compared with the others.

why.stone: The heavy wedge-serif forms feel solid and engraved, though rather like Victorian print.
why.carving: The serifs are sharp, cut wedges, but the bowls and curves are smooth ink rather than faceted.
why.calm: The dark weight and very bold display lines feel heavy and somewhat loud.
why.personality: The wedge serifs and the odd g give it a distinct, old-fashioned character.
why.inscription: The capitals are heavy and closely spaced, closer to a display serif than to Roman inscriptional caps.
why.oblique: A proper italic with a consistent slant, but the dark colour makes the notes lines heavy.
why.small: The 13 px text is legible but dark and slightly dense.

why.stone: A neutral grotesque sans with no lapidary quality at all.
why.carving: Perfectly smooth, engineered curves at every display size.
why.calm: Quiet and orderly, but the heavy bold numbers feel technical rather than grounded.
why.personality: Competent but generic UI sans; nothing ties it to stone or Sisyphus.
why.inscription: Monoline grotesque capitals have none of the Roman inscriptional stroke or proportion.
why.oblique: Clean, consistent italic with true italic forms, clearly distinct and readable at 13 px.
why.small: Very open, sharp and even at 13 px; the most comfortable small text of the set.

why.stone: A clean grotesque sans with no lapidary quality at all.
why.carving: Perfectly smooth, engineered outlines with no cuts or facets.
why.calm: Neutral and orderly, quiet though somewhat cold and technical.
why.personality: Generic UI sans; competent but forgettable for this voice.
why.inscription: Monoline sans capitals with no inscriptional proportion or stroke.
why.oblique: Consistent, even italic clearly distinct from the upright, readable as emphasis.
why.small: 13 px text is the clearest and most open of the set.

why.stone: A neutral grotesque sans that reads as screen UI, with nothing lapidary about it.
why.carving: The display sizes have smooth, mechanical curves with no facets or chiselled terminals.
why.calm: The rhythm is even and orderly, though the bold numbers have a slightly technical, assertive feel.
why.personality: A generic corporate sans that could belong to any app.
why.inscription: Monoline grotesque capitals bear no relation to Roman inscriptional capitals.
why.oblique: The italic is clean, consistent and distinct, with even colour, but a little cold.
why.small: The 13 px text is open, crisp and very comfortable to read.

why.stone: Clearly lapidary, Trajan-like capital letterforms evoke carved monuments.
why.carving: Despite the inscriptional shapes the outlines are smooth and drawn, with no visible facets.
why.calm: Dignified in plain titles, but the swash capitals and all-caps body become theatrical and busy.
why.personality: Very memorable, but its movie-poster classicism risks overwhelming a quiet app.
why.inscription: Regular capitals have true Roman proportions, though the swash variants (bold MOBILITÀ, italic SISIFO · ROCK) undercut the dignity.
why.oblique: Italic small caps look like a mechanical skew and are hard to read as running emphasis.
why.small: 13 px text sets entirely in small caps, which is tiring and unsuitable for body copy.

why.stone: Flared, incised-looking all-caps letters evoke engraved inscriptions strongly.
why.carving: Flared terminals suggest a chisel, but the curves are smooth rather than faceted.
why.calm: Swashy bold caps with ligatures and unusual forms feel ornate and restless.
why.personality: Very distinctive and classical, though leaning decorative and fantasy-like.
why.inscription: Regular caps have true Roman inscriptional proportions; the bold swashes undercut the dignity.
why.oblique: Italic small caps and swash forms are wiry and fussy, hard to read as 13 px emphasis.
why.small: There is no lowercase, so 13 px running text sets in caps and small caps and reads poorly.

why.stone: The all-capital classical forms evoke engraved lettering, even though the overall effect is more ornamental than solid.
why.carving: The curves and terminals are smooth and refined, with no visible chisel facets.
why.calm: The swashed bold capitals and caps-only body text make the page busy and theatrical.
why.personality: It is very distinctive, though the decorative flourishes push it toward fantasy rather than quiet stone.
why.inscription: The regular capitals have good Roman proportions and dignity, but the bold weight turns into decorative swashes.
why.oblique: The italic is a slanted small-caps texture with flourishes, so it barely reads as emphasis and is awkward at 13 px.
why.small: The 13 px body set entirely in small capitals is tiring and hard to scan at phone size.
